ACKR.a: The American Cocker Spaniel is a breed of sporting dog. It is a spaniel type dog that is closely related to the English Cocker Spaniel; the two breeds diverged during the 20th century due to differing breed standards in the US and the UK.
ACKR.h: The word spanyell is thought to date from the late 12th century when it was used to name a type of dog imported into England from Spain, with the span part of the word referring to the country of origin.

AESK.a: The American Eskimo Dog is a breed of companion dog, originating in Germany.
AESK.h: In Northern Europe, smaller Spitz were eventually developed into the various German Spitz breeds.

AFGH.a: The Afghan Hound is a hound distinguished by its thick, fine, silky coat, and a tail with a ring curl at the end.
AFGH.h: The Afghan Hound has been identified as a basal breed that predates the emergence of the modern breeds in the 19th century.

AHRT.a: The American Hairless Terrier is a breed of companion dog from the United States that was developed from naturally hairless Rat Terriers.
AHRT.h: In 1972, a completely hairless bitch pup was whelped in a litter of purebred Rat Terriers and adopted by Willie and Edwin Scott of Louisiana.

AIRT.a: The Airedale Terrier, also called Bingley Terrier and Waterside Terrier, is a dog breed of the terrier type that originated in the valley (dale) of the River Aire, in the West Riding of Yorkshire, England.
AIRT.h: Airedale, a valley (dale) in the West Riding of Yorkshire, named for the River Aire that runs through it, was the birthplace of the breed.

akc:affenpinscher.a: The Affenpinscher is a German breed of small toy dog of Pinscher type.
akc:affenpinscher.h: The word 'Affenpinscher' derives from Affe, German for 'ape' or 'monkey'; it is sometimes translated as 'Monkey Terrier', although the dog is a Pinscher and not a terrier.

akc:american-english-coonhound.a: The American English Coonhound, also referred to as the English Coonhound or the Redtick Coonhound, is a breed of coonhound that originated in and is typically bred in the Southern United States.
akc:american-english-coonhound.h: The breed's ancestry can be traced back to foxhounds brought to the United States by European settlers during the 17th and 18th centuries.

akc:american-foxhound.a: The American Foxhound is a breed of dog, closely related to the English Foxhound.
akc:american-foxhound.h: In 1650, Robert Brooke sailed from England to Maryland with his pack of hunting dogs, which were the root of several strains of American hounds.

akc:american-water-spaniel.a: The American Water Spaniel is a breed of spaniel which originated in the United States.
akc:american-water-spaniel.h: Originating in Wisconsin, the American Water Spaniel is the Wisconsin state dog.

akc:barbet.a: The Barbet is a medium-sized breed of French water dog. It is a rare breed.
akc:barbet.h: The Barbet as it is known today is a fairly rare and recent breed development.

akc:beauceron.a: The Beauceron is a herding dog breed originating from the plains of Central France.
akc:beauceron.h: The breed originated as a herding dog in France. It was first mentioned in 1587, and named as the "Berger de Beauce" in 1809.

akc:belgian-laekenois.a: The Belgian Shepherd, also known as the Belgian Sheepdog or the Chien de Berger Belge, is a Belgian breed of herding dog of medium size.
akc:belgian-laekenois.h: The Belgian Shepherd descends from the same common type of herding dog as similar Western European breeds such as the Bouvier des Ardennes, the Dutch Shepherd and the German Shepherd, and for centuries was used by Belgian shepherds for this task.

akc:bergamasco-sheepdog.a: The Bergamasco Shepherd, also known as the Bergamasco Sheepdog and in Italian: Cane da Pastore Bergamasco, is an Italian breed of sheepdog.
akc:bergamasco-sheepdog.h: The origins of the Pastore Bergamasco are unknown. In 1781, G. von Albertini described Bergamasco shepherds on the Splügenberg using large dogs with long, wool-like hair to guard and drive their flocks; during migration, individual dogs could be entrusted with groups of sheep.

akc:biewer-terrier.a: The Biewer Terrier is a toy dog of German descent that is the result of two Yorkshire Terriers with a recessive piebald gene breeding.
akc:biewer-terrier.h: The Biewer Terrier was first bred in Germany in 1984 by breeders Werner and Gertrude Biewer after two tricolor puppies were born in their kennel.

akc:black-and-tan-coonhound.a: The Black and Tan Coonhound is a breed of hunting dog. Developed in the United States from crosses between the Bloodhound and the Black and Tan Virginia Foxhound, this scent hound runs its game entirely by scent and is used primarily for raccoon hunting.
akc:black-and-tan-coonhound.h: The Black and Tan Coonhound is descended from the Talbot Hound, found in medieval England after the 11th century.

akc:bluetick-coonhound.a: The Bluetick Coonhound is a breed of coonhound originating in the United States.
akc:bluetick-coonhound.h: The Bluetick Coonhound, which originated in Louisiana, was developed from the Grand Bleu de Gascogne hound of southwestern France, as well as the English Foxhound, the cur dog, the American Foxhound, and the Black and Tan Virginia Foxhound.

akc:boykin-spaniel.a: The Boykin Spaniel is a medium-sized breed of dog, a Spaniel bred for hunting wild turkeys and ducks in the Wateree River Swamp of South Carolina, in the United States.
akc:boykin-spaniel.h: The first Boykin Spaniel, or the precursor of today's breed, was reportedly a small, stray spaniel type dog that befriended a banker walking from his home to the First Presbyterian Church in Spartanburg, South Carolina around 1900.

akc:bracco-italiano.a: The Bracco Italiano is an Italian breed of pointing dog.
akc:bracco-italiano.h: The Bracco Italiano is the traditional pointer of the Italian peninsula.

akc:canaan-dog.a: The Canaan Dog is a dog breed developed in the early 20th century from semiwild pariah dogs that were the descendants of animals present in the region since biblical times.
akc:canaan-dog.h: Canaan dogs, or dogs nearly identical, were also found in Syria over 9,000 years ago.

akc:cesky-terrier.a: The Cesky Terrier is a small terrier type dog originating in Czechoslovakia.
akc:cesky-terrier.h: The Cesky Terrier was created by a Czech breeder, František Horák, in 1948, as a cross between a Sealyham Terrier and a Scottish Terrier, to create a terrier suitable for hunting in the forests of Bohemia.

akc:chesapeake-bay-retriever.a: The Chesapeake Bay Retriever is a large breed of dog belonging to the retriever, gundog, and sporting breed groups.
akc:chesapeake-bay-retriever.h: Chesapeake Bay Retrievers trace their history to two pups who were rescued from a foundering ship in Maryland in 1807.

akc:clumber-spaniel.a: The Clumber Spaniel is a breed of dog of the spaniel type, developed in the United Kingdom.
akc:clumber-spaniel.h: The breed's history is uncertain before the middle of the 19th century.

akc:dandie-dinmont-terrier.a: A Dandie Dinmont Terrier is a small Scottish dog breed in the terrier family.
akc:dandie-dinmont-terrier.h: The breed originates from the dogs being used in the Anglo-Scottish border country.

akc:danish-swedish-farmdog.a: Danish–Swedish Farmdog, historically known as the Danish Pinscher, is a breed of dog that has its origin in Denmark and southern Sweden, but has become popular all over Scandinavia, serving as a multi-purpose dog breed.
akc:danish-swedish-farmdog.h: The Danish–Swedish Farmdog may have originated in Scania, in the region of Skåneland.

akc:dogo-argentino.a: The Dogo Argentino is an Argentine breed of large dog of mastiff type.
akc:dogo-argentino.h: In the 1920s Antonio Nores Martinez, a young student of Córdoba in central Argentina, set out with his brother Augustin Nores Martinez to create a new breed of big game hunting dog, especially wild boar.

akc:english-foxhound.a: The English Foxhound is one of the four foxhound breeds of dog. It is a cousin of the American Foxhound.
akc:english-foxhound.h: The English Foxhound has been bred for over two hundred years, with the stud books dating back before 1800.

akc:english-toy-spaniel.a: The King Charles Spaniel is a small dog breed of the spaniel type. In 1903, The Kennel Club combined four separate toy spaniel breeds under this single title.
akc:english-toy-spaniel.h: The fact that dogs are always part of a royal Japanese present suggested to the Commodore the thought that possibly one species of spaniel now in England may be traced to a Japanese origin.

akc:entlebucher-mountain-dog.a: The Entlebucher Sennenhund or Entlebucher Mountain Dog is a medium-sized herding dog, it is the smallest of the four regional breeds that constitute the Sennenhund dog type.
akc:entlebucher-mountain-dog.h: The Entlebucher is the smallest of four Swiss mountain dogs, the others being the Appenzeller Sennenhund, the Bernese Mountain Dog, and the Greater Swiss Mountain Dog.

akc:finnish-lapphund.a: The Finnish Lapphund is a hardy, easy-going, medium-size breed of Spitz type.
akc:finnish-lapphund.h: The breed has its origins as a reindeer herder of the Sami people. The Sami are an indigenous people residing in areas now divided between Finland, Sweden, Norway, and Russia.

akc:german-pinscher.a: The German Pinscher or Deutscher Pinscher is a German breed of dog in the Pinscher and Schnauzer group.
akc:german-pinscher.h: The origins of the German Pinscher are unknown. Dogs of this type, both rough-haired and smooth-haired, were traditionally kept as carriage dogs or as stable dogs, and so were sometimes known as Stallpinscher; they were capable ratters.

akc:grand-basset-griffon-vendeen.a: The Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen or GBGV is a dog breed from France.
akc:grand-basset-griffon-vendeen.h: The Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen is derived from the Grand Griffon. The first selections were made at the end of the 19th century by the Comte d'Elva who was looking for subjects with "straight legs".

akc:harrier.a: The Harrier is a medium-sized dog breed of the hound class, used for hunting hares by trailing them.
akc:harrier.h: Sources have widely conflicting stories about the origins of this breed.

akc:irish-red-and-white-setter.a: The Irish Red and White Setter is a breed of dog. As with all setters, it is classified as a gundog in the UK and is included in the sporting group in America and Canada.
akc:irish-red-and-white-setter.h: 'Setting dogges' – an ancient term for setters, were developed to find game birds and would have been used in Roman times.

akc:lagotto-romagnolo.a: The Lagotto Romagnolo is an Italian breed of dog. It is a traditional breed of the once-extensive marshlands of the Delta del Po, in the eastern part of the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy, where it was used as a gun dog, specifically as a water retriever.
akc:lagotto-romagnolo.h: The Lagotto originated in the once-extensive marshlands and lagoons of the Delta del Po, in areas such as Comacchio and Ravenna, in the eastern part of the historical Romagna region of Italy, now part of Emilia-Romagna.

akc:lakeland-terrier.a: The Lakeland Terrier is a dog breed, which takes its name from its place of origin, the Lake District in England.
akc:lakeland-terrier.h: As one of the earliest Terriers (Latin derivation of earth), dating from the 1700s, this "earth" dog is a descendant of the old English Black and Tan and Fell Terriers.

akc:lancashire-heeler.a: The Lancashire Heeler is a small breed of dog developed for use as a drover and herder of cattle.
akc:lancashire-heeler.h: It is generally accepted that the Lancashire Heeler is descended from the Welsh Corgi and the Manchester Terrier in England.

akc:lowchen.a: The Löwchen or Little Lion Dog is a breed of small dog. The Löwchen once had the dubious distinction, like the Portuguese Water Dog and the Havanese, of being the rarest dog in the world.
akc:lowchen.h: The breed is found in many countries as far back as the sixteenth century.

akc:manchester-terrier-standard.a: The Manchester Terrier is a breed of dog of the smooth-haired terrier type.
akc:manchester-terrier-standard.h: The Manchester Terrier was developed from the Black and Tan Terrier and the Whippet..

akc:miniature-american-shepherd.a: The Miniature American Shepherd, frequently abbreviated MAS, is a small herding dog breed.
akc:miniature-american-shepherd.h: The MAS was bred first in the United States as a small herding and working dog.

akc:mudi.a: The Mudi is a herding dog breed from Hungary. It is closely related to the Puli and Pumi, from which it was separated in the 1930s.
akc:mudi.h: The Mudi was first discovered as a breed in 1936 by Dr Dezso Fenyes in Hungary, where it became known as the "driver dog".

akc:nederlandse-kooikerhondje.a: The Kooikerhondje is a small spaniel-type dog breed of Dutch ancestry that was originally used as a working dog, particularly in a decoy to lure ducks.
akc:nederlandse-kooikerhondje.h: The Kooikerhondje was developed in the Netherlands sometime around the 16th century in order to lure ducks into duck decoys where hunters could easily catch the fowl.

akc:norwegian-buhund.a: The Norwegian Buhund is a breed of dog of the spitz type. It is closely related to the Icelandic Sheepdog and the Jämthund.
akc:norwegian-buhund.h: The Norwegian Buhund belongs to a large class of dogs called the Spitz type.

akc:norwegian-lundehund.a: The Norwegian Lundehund is a small dog breed of the Spitz type that originates from Norway.
akc:norwegian-lundehund.h: The Lundehund was a valuable working animal for hunting puffin birds along the Norwegian coast as food for over 400 years.
akc:norwegian-lundehund.wt: 7–8 kilograms (15–18 lb; males), 5–6 kilograms (11–13 lb; females)

akc:plott-hound.a: The Plott Hound, often referred to as the Plott, is a large scent hound, originally bred for hunting bears.
akc:plott-hound.h: Of the seven breeds of United Kennel Club (UKC) registered coonhounds, the Plott Hound is the only one that does not trace its ancestry to the foxhound.

akc:pointer.a: The Pointer, sometimes called the English Pointer, is a medium-sized breed of pointing dog developed in England.
akc:pointer.h: There has been much debate among dog historians about the ancestry of the Pointer.

akc:polish-lowland-sheepdog.a: The Polish Lowland Sheepdog, is a medium-sized, shaggy-coated, sheep dog breed native to Poland.
akc:polish-lowland-sheepdog.h: Known in its present form in Poland from at least the thirteenth century, the PON is most likely descended from the Puli, Tibetan Terrier and the herding dogs.

akc:portuguese-podengo.a: The Portuguese Podengo, also known as the Podengo Português or Portuguese Warren Hound, is a Portuguese breed of dog of warren hound type.
akc:portuguese-podengo.h: In the Middle Ages, hunting dogs in Portugal were collectively known as Podengos de Mostra ('pointers'}.

akc:pyrenean-shepherd.a: The Pyrenean Sheepdog, the Chien de Berger des Pyrénées in French, is a small to medium-sized breed of herding dog from the Pyrenees Mountains region of France.
akc:pyrenean-shepherd.h: The Pyrenean Sheepdog is found along the entire length of the French Pyrenees and is even known in Basque Country to the west.

akc:russell-terrier.a: The Russell Terrier is a predominantly white working terrier with an instinct to hunt prey underground.
akc:russell-terrier.h: The name Jack Russell Terrier was never used to describe a breed of dog.

akc:russian-toy.a: The Russian Toy is a very small breed of dog originally bred in Russia from the English Toy Terrier.
akc:russian-toy.h: The first evidence of English-style terriers in Russia can be seen in the Museum of Zoology in Saint Petersburg.

akc:sealyham-terrier.a: The Sealyham Terrier is a rare Welsh breed of small to medium-sized terrier that originated in Wales as a working dog.
akc:sealyham-terrier.h: The breed was developed between 1850 and 1891 by Captain John Edwardes, at Sealyham House, near Wolfscastle in the Welsh county of Pembrokeshire.
akc:sealyham-terrier.wt: 9 kilograms (20 lb; males), 8 kilograms (18 lb; females)

akc:skye-terrier.a: The Skye Terrier is a Scottish breed of terrier. It is long, low, hardy and short-legged, and in the twenty-first century is among the most endangered breeds of the United Kingdom.
akc:skye-terrier.h: A colour lithograph of Skye Terriers was included in The Illustrated Book of the Dog by Vero Shaw in 1881.

akc:smooth-fox-terrier.a: The Smooth Fox Terrier is a breed of dog, one of many terrier breeds. It was the first breed in the Fox Terrier family to be given official recognition by The Kennel Club.
akc:smooth-fox-terrier.h: The Smooth Fox Terrier's development as a breed is largely undocumented, but the dog has been known as a distinct breed in England since at least the 18th century; the first documented evidence of the Smooth Fox Terrier came in 1790, when a Colonel Thornton painted a portrait of his dog, Pitch.

akc:spanish-water-dog.a: The Spanish Water Dog or Perro de Agua Español is a Spanish breed of water dog.
akc:spanish-water-dog.h: The Perro de Agua is a traditional dog population of Spain. It was always a minority breed, present in smaller numbers than some other Spanish dogs.

akc:sussex-spaniel.a: The Sussex Spaniel is a breed of dog native to Sussex, in southern England.
akc:sussex-spaniel.h: The Sussex is a native breed to the county, known to be bred at Goodwood, West Sussex in 1792 and by Augustus Elliot Fuller of Rose Hill (now known as Brightling Park, Brightling in East Sussex, England).

akc:treeing-walker-coonhound.a: The Treeing Walker Coonhound is a breed of hound descended primarily from English and American Foxhounds.
akc:treeing-walker-coonhound.h: The Treeing Walker Coonhound was developed in the 19th century. John W. Walker and George Washington Maupin, two breeders from Kentucky, are credited with the breed's initial development through the selective breeding of foxhounds.

akc:welsh-springer-spaniel.a: The Welsh Springer Spaniel is a breed of dog and a member of the spaniel family.
akc:welsh-springer-spaniel.h: The origin of the Welsh Springer Spaniel is unknown, but dogs resembling the breed with its distinctive red and white coat are frequently depicted in old pictures and prints.

akc:welsh-terrier.a: The Welsh Terrier also known as the Welshie, is believed to have originated in the 1700s in Wales and was originally bred for hunting fox, rodents and badger; in the remote mountains of northern Wales, but during the last century, it has mainly been bred for showing.

akc:wirehaired-vizsla.a: The Hungarian Wirehaired Vizsla or Hungarian Wirehaired Pointer is a Hungarian breed of pointer dog.
akc:wirehaired-vizsla.h: The Hungarian Wirehaired Vizsla is a completely separate breed from the more commonly known shorthaired Vizsla.

AKIT.a: The Akita Inu is a Japanese dog breed of large size. Originating from the mountains of northern Japan, the Akita has a short double coat similar to that of many other northern spitz breeds.
AKIT.h: The direct ancestor of the Akita Inu was a dog kept as a guard dog and fighting dog by samurai and wealthy farmers in the Ōdate area, and was known as the Ōdate dog (大館犬) until 1931 when it was renamed the Akita Inu.

AMAL.a: The Alaskan Malamute is a large spitz-type breed of dog that was originally bred for its strength and endurance to haul heavy freight as a sled dog.
AMAL.h: The Alaskan Malamute had a prominent role with their human companions as a utilitarian dog, working, hunting, and living alongside humans.
AMAL.wt: 38 kilograms (84 lb; males), 34 kilograms (75 lb; females)

AMST.a: The American Staffordshire Terrier, also known as the AmStaff, is a medium-sized, short-coated American dog breed recognized by the American Kennel Club, but not the United Kennel Club, which instead allows American Staffordshire Terriers to be registered under the American Pit Bull Terrier breed.
AMST.h: Some varieties of the extinct bull-and-terrier dog from the British Isles began to find their way into America as early as 1850.

ANAT.a: The Kangal Shepherd Dog or Turkish Kangal is a traditional Turkish breed of large livestock guardian dog.
ANAT.h: The word Kangal is of Turkic origin, sharing same etymological roots with Kangly tribe, the ethnonym has been linked to the Turkic word kang, meaning wagon or cart.

AUCD.a: The Australian Cattle Dog, or simply Cattle Dog, is a breed of herding dog developed in Australia for droving cattle over long distances across rough terrain.
AUCD.h: British colonist George Hall and his family arrived in the New South Wales Colony in 1802.

AUSS.a: The Australian Shepherd, also known as the Aussie, is a breed of herding dog from the United States.
AUSS.h: The Australian Shepherd descends in part from pastoral dogs brought to herd Spanish flocks in North America as early as the 1500s.

AUST.a: The Australian Terrier is a small breed of dog of the terrier type. The breed was developed in Australia, although the ancestral types of dogs from which the breed descends were from Great Britain.
AUST.h: The Australian Terrier is descended from the rough coated type terriers brought from Great Britain to Australia in the early 19th century.

AZWK.a: The Azawakh is a breed of dog from West Africa. With ancient origins, it is raised throughout the Sahelian zone of Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso.

BASS.a: The Basset Hound is a short-legged breed of scent hound. The Basset Hound was developed in Great Britain from several now-extinct strains of French basset breeds.
BASS.h: The Basset type originated in France, and is descended from the 6th-century hounds belonging to St Hubert of Belgium, which through breeding at the Benedictine Abbey of St. Hubert eventually became what is known as the St Hubert's Hound around 1000 AD.

BEAG.a: The Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
BEAG.h: The origin of the Beagle is uncertain. In the 11th century, William the Conqueror brought the St. Hubert Hound and the Talbot hound to Britain.

BEDT.a: The Bedlington Terrier is a breed of small dog named after the mining town of Bedlington, Northumberland in North East England.
BEDT.h: Bred in the village of Bedlington in Northumberland, the Bedlington Terrier has been described as "the favourite companion of the northern miners".

BELS.a: The Belgian Shepherd, also known as the Belgian Sheepdog or the Chien de Berger Belge, is a Belgian breed of herding dog of medium size.
BELS.h: The Belgian Shepherd descends from the same common type of herding dog as similar Western European breeds such as the Bouvier des Ardennes, the Dutch Shepherd and the German Shepherd, and for centuries was used by Belgian shepherds for this task.

BERD.a: The Bearded Collie, also called Beardie, Highland Collie, or Hairy Mountain Dog is a British breed of herding dog of the collie type.
BERD.h: The legend of the Bearded Collie's origin is that the ancestors of what became the Polish Lowland Sheepdog were abandoned on the shores of Scotland, and these dogs then bred with native herding dogs.

BICH.a: The Bichon Frisé or Bichon à Poil Frisé is a Franco-Belgian breed of small toy dog of bichon type.
BICH.h: The dogs found early success in Spain and it is generally believed that Spanish seamen introduced the early breed to Tenerife in the Canary Islands.

BLDH.a: The bloodhound is a large scent hound, originally bred for hunting deer, wild boar, rabbits, and since the Middle Ages, for tracking people.
BLDH.h: The St. Hubert Hound was, according to legend, first bred ca. AD 1000 by monks at the Saint-Hubert Monastery in Belgium; its likely origins are in France, home of many of modern hounds.

BMAL.a: The Belgian Shepherd, also known as the Belgian Sheepdog or the Chien de Berger Belge, is a Belgian breed of herding dog of medium size.
BMAL.h: The Belgian Shepherd descends from the same common type of herding dog as similar Western European breeds such as the Bouvier des Ardennes, the Dutch Shepherd and the German Shepherd, and for centuries was used by Belgian shepherds for this task.

BMD.a: The Bernese Mountain Dog, German: Berner Sennenhund or Dürrbächler, is a large dog breed originating from the canton of Bern, Switzerland and the Swiss Alps.
BMD.h: Historically, in some locales at least, the breed was called a Dürrbachhund or Dürrbächler, for a small town (Dürrbach) where the large dogs were especially frequent.

BOER.a: The Boerboel is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
BOER.h: The name Boerboel derives from the Afrikaans words boer, meaning farmer, and boel, a shortening of boelhond, meaning bulldog.

BORD.a: The Border Collie is a breed of British herding dog of the collie type of medium size.
BORD.h: In a study done by Grant on a hillfort named Danebury, today's collie is mentioned as a comparator for dogs of the type used by Celtic herders.

BORT.a: The Border Terrier is a British breed of small, rough-coated terrier. It originates from the area of the Anglo-Scottish border, and shares ancestry with the Dandie Dinmont Terrier and the Bedlington Terrier from the same area.
BORT.h: Originally the Border Terrier was referred to as the Coquetdale Terrier or Redesdale Terrier from the area in which it evolved, but by the late 1800s it was generally known as the Border Terrier, probably because of its long history with the Border Hunt in Northumberland.

BORZ.a: The Borzoi or Russian Hunting Sighthound is a Russian breed of hunting dog of the sighthound type.
BORZ.h: The Borzoi originated in the sixteenth century Russia by crossing Saluki and European sighthounds with thick-coated Russian breeds.

BOST.a: The Boston Terrier is a breed of dog originating in the United States of America.
BOST.h: The Boston terrier breed originated around 1870, when Robert C. Hooper of Boston purchased from a man named William O'Brien a dog named Judge (known later as Hooper's Judge), which was of a bull and terrier type lineage.

BOUV.a: The Bouvier des Flandres is a herding dog breed originating in Flanders, Belgium.
BOUV.h: The monks at the Ter Duinen monastery were among the earliest known dog breeders in Flanders.

BOX.a: The Boxer is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.
BOX.h: The Boxer is a hunting mastiff developed in Germany in the late 19th century from the now extinct Bullenbeisser, a dog of English Mastiff descent, and Bulldogs brought in from Great Britain.

BPIC.a: The Berger Picard or Picardy Shepherd, is a French herding dog originating in Picardy.
BPIC.h: In 2018 a genetic study found that, just prior to 1859, a broadly distributed European herding dog had given rise to the French Berger Picard, the German Shepherd Dog, and the five Italian herding breeds: the Bergamasco Shepherd Dog, Cane Paratore, Lupino del Gigante, Pastore d'Oropa, and the Pastore della Lessinia e del Lagorai.

BRIA.a: The Briard or Berger de Brie is a French breed of large shepherd dog, traditionally used both for herding sheep and to defend them.
BRIA.h: The Briard originated in, and is named for, the Brie historic region of north-central France, where it was traditionally used both for herding sheep and to defend them.

BRIT.a: The Brittany Spaniel or Breton Spaniel is a French breed of gun dog of spaniel type, bred primarily for bird hunting.
BRIT.h: The Brittany Spaniel originated in the Brittany region of north-western France, for which it is named.

BRTR.a: The Black Russian Terrier, also known as the Chornyi Terrier, is a breed of dog from the USSR.
BRTR.h: The Black Russian Terrier was developed in the former USSR in Red Star (Krasnaya Zvezda) Kennel by the state for use as a military/working dogs.
BRTR.ht: 72–76 centimetres (28–30 in; males), 68–72 centimetres (27–28 in; females)
BRTR.wt: 50–60 kilograms (110–130 lb; males), 45–50 kilograms (99–110 lb; females)

BRUS.a: The Griffon Bruxellois or Brussels Griffon is a breed of toy dog, named for their city of origin of Brussels, Belgium.
BRUS.h: The three variations of the Griffon Bruxellois, the Brussels Griffon (Griffon Bruxellois), the Belgian Griffon (Griffon Belge), and the Petit Brabançon, all descend from dog called a Smousje, a rough coated, small terrier-like dog kept in stables to eliminate rodents, similar to the Dutch Smoushond.

BSJI.a: The Basenji is a breed of hunting dog created from stock that originated in Central Africa, including in the Republic of the Congo and other adjacent tropical African countries.
BSJI.h: The Basenji originated on the continent of Africa, where it has been identified with Egyptian depictions of dogs with curled tails and erect ears, a breed called Tesem which is found in murals as old as 4,500 years.

BULD.a: The Bulldog is a British breed of dog of mastiff type. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.
BULD.h: The first reference to the word "Bulldog" is dated 1631 or 1632 in a letter by a man named Preswick Eaton where he writes: "procuer mee two good Bulldogs, and let them be sent by ye first shipp".

BULM.a: The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
BULM.h: The origins of the Bullmastiff are unclear. In the 18th century, in some regions of England, the English Mastiff and Old English Bulldog were commonly inter-bred to produce dogs suitable for guarding people and their property.

BULT.a: The Bull Terrier is a breed of dog in the terrier family. There is also a miniature version of this breed, the Miniature Bull Terrier.
BULT.h: At the start of the 19th century, the "bull and terrier" breeds were developed to satisfy the needs for vermin control and animal-based blood sports.

CAIR.a: The Cairn Terrier is a terrier breed originating in the Scottish Highlands and recognised as one of Scotland's earliest working dogs.
CAIR.h: Cairn Terriers originated in the Scottish Highlands and the Isle of Skye.

CANE.a: The Cane Corso is an Italian breed of mastiff. It is usually kept as a companion dog or guard dog; it may also be used to protect livestock.
CANE.h: According to the breed standard of the Fédération Cynologique Internationale, the Cane Corso was once distributed throughout much of the Italian peninsula, but in the recent past was found only in Puglia, in southern Italy.

CARD.a: The Cardigan Welsh Corgi is one of two different varieties of livestock-herding dog breeds known as Welsh Corgis, with the other being the Pembroke Welsh Corgi.
CARD.h: Pembroke Welsh and Cardigan Welsh Corgis were both originally listed as one breed by The Kennel Club (UK) in 1925; the two varieties were officially recognized as distinct from one another by The Kennel Club by 1928, but were still categorized together under the title of "Welsh Corgis".

CCRT.a: The Curly-coated Retriever is a breed of dog originally bred in England for upland bird and waterfowl hunting.

CHIH.a: The Chihuahua or Chihuahueño is a Mexican breed of toy dog and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world.
CHIH.h: DNA studies suggest that native American dogs entered North America from Siberia approximately 10,000 years ago and were subsequently isolated from other breeds for approximately 9,000 years until the arrival of the first Europeans; these pre-contact dogs exhibited a unique genetic signature that is now nearly extinct.

CHIN.a: The Japanese Chin, also known as the Japanese Spaniel, is a toy dog breed, being both a lap dog and a companion dog, with a distinctive heritage.
CHIN.h: While most believe that the source breed for the Japanese Chin originated in China, the route by which the Chin arrived in Japan is a widely debated topic.

CHOW.a: The Chow Chow is a spitz-type of dog breed originally from Northern China.
CHOW.h: The Chow Chow has been identified as a basal breed that predates the emergence of the modern breeds in the 19th century.

CIRN.a: The Cirneco dell'Etna is an Italian breed of hunting dog from the Mediterranean island of Sicily.
CIRN.h: The Cirneco is a traditional warren hound of Sicily. It is commonly claimed that it is an ancient breed, with origins in Ancient Egypt or Phoenicia; according to the Ente Nazionale della Cinofilia Italiana, coins and inscriptions document its presence in the island from before the time of Christ.

CKCS.a: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel (CKCS) is a British breed of toy dog of spaniel type.
CKCS.h: During the early part of the 18th century, John Churchill, 1st Duke of Marlborough, kept red and white King Charles type spaniels for hunting.

COLL.a: Collies form a distinctive type of herding dogs, including many related landraces and standardized breeds.

COOK.a: The Chinook is a breed of sled dog, developed in the state of New Hampshire during the early 20th century.
COOK.h: The Chinook owes its existence to one man: Arthur Treadwell Walden of Wonalancet, New Hampshire.

COTO.a: The Coton de Tuléar is a breed of small dog named for the city of Tuléar in Madagascar.
COTO.h: The Coton de Tuléar developed on the island of Madagascar and is still the island's national dog.

CPAT.a: The Cane Paratore is a breed of herding dog from Italy. The breed primarily exists in its traditional role in Abruzzo, its historical region of origin, having not gained popularity from outside dog fanciers.
CPAT.h: The name Cane Paratore, sometimes called the Cane Toccatore, comes from an Italian dialect where "Paratore" translates to "to stand in front" or "to touch." The meaning is rooted from the breed's integral role of aiding in farming practices as a herding dog by moving livestock through less aggressive methods, such as light touches or standing in the path of livestock.

CRES.a: The Chinese Crested Dog is a hairless breed of dog. Like most hairless dog breeds, the Chinese Crested Dog comes in two varieties, without hair and with hair, which can be born in the same litter: the hairless and the powderpuff.
CRES.h: Although hairless dogs have been found in many places in the world, it is unlikely that the origins of the modern Chinese Crested Dog are in China.

DACH.a: The Dachshund, also known as the Dackel or Teckel, is a German breed of short-legged, long-bodied dog of hound type.
DACH.h: The Dachshund is a creation of German breeders and includes elements of German, French, and English hounds and terriers.

DALM.a: The Dalmatian is a breed of dog with a white coat marked with dark-coloured spots.
DALM.h: The Fédération Cynologique Internationale (FCI) recognized Croatia as its country of origin, citing several historical sources.

DANE.a: The Great Dane is a German breed of large mastiff-sighthound, which descends from hunting dogs of the Middle Ages used to hunt bears, wild boar, and deer.
DANE.h: In the sixteenth century the nobility in many countries of Europe imported strong, long-legged dogs of different sizes and phenotypes, some of mastiff or greyhound type, from England and Ireland.

DDBX.a: The Dogue de Bordeaux, also known as the Bordeaux Mastiff, French Mastiff or Bordeauxdog, is a large French mastiff breed.
DDBX.h: The Dogue de Bordeaux was known in France as early as the 14th century, particularly in southern France in the region around Bordeaux.

DEER.a: The Scottish Deerhound, or simply the Deerhound, is a breed of large sighthound, once bred to hunt the red deer by coursing.
DEER.h: The Hilton of Cadboll Stone dates from around 1200 years ago, and depicts at the bottom of the panel a deer being chased by two large dogs and two armed horsemen.

DOBP.a: The Dobermann is a German breed of working dog of pinscher type. In Canada and the United States it is known as the Doberman Pinscher.
DOBP.h: Dobermanns were first bred in the 1880s by Karl Friedrich Louis Dobermann, a tax collector who ran a dog pound in Apolda in present-day Thuringia in central Germany.

ECKR.a: The English Cocker Spaniel is a breed of gun dog. It is noteworthy for producing one of the most varied numbers of pups in a litter among all dog breeds.
ECKR.h: Spaniel type dogs have been found in art and literature for almost 500 years.

ESET.a: The English Setter is a medium-size breed of dog. It is part of the setter group, which includes the red Irish Setters, Irish Red and White Setters, and black-and-tan Gordon Setters.

ESSP.a: The English Springer Spaniel is a breed of gun dog in the Spaniel group traditionally used for flushing and retrieving game.
ESSP.h: The English physician John Caius described the spaniel in his book the Treatise of Englishe Dogs published in 1576.

EURA.a: The Eurasier, or Eurasian, is a spitz type breed of dog that originated in Germany through cross-breeding between popular European and Asian Spitz.
EURA.h: Eurasiers originated in Germany in 1960, when the founder, Julius Wipfel, set out together with Charlotte Baldamus and a small group of enthusiasts to create a breed with the best qualities of the Chow Chow and the Wolfspitz.

FBUL.a: The French Bulldog Commonly known as a Frenchie, is a French breed of companion dog or toy dog.
FBUL.h: From the beginning of the nineteenth century, bulldogs were bred in the United Kingdom for purposes other than traditional blood sports such as bull-baiting, which were banned in 1835.

FCR.a: The Flat-coated Retriever is a gun dog breed originating from England.
FCR.h: Originating in the mid-19th century in England, the Flat-Coated Retriever gained popularity as a gamekeeper's dog.

FIEL.a: The Field Spaniel is a medium-sized dog breed of spaniel type. They were originally developed to be all-black show dogs in the late 19th and early 20th centuries and were unpopular for work as a hunting dog.
FIEL.h: The Field Spaniel was originally developed for the show ring by competitors who were attempting to develop an all-black Spaniel.

FINS.a: The Finnish Spitz is a breed of dog originating in Finland. The breed was originally trained to hunt all types of game from squirrels and other rodents to bears.
FINS.h: It is assumed that the Finnish Spitz developed from Spitz-type dogs that came from central Russia with migrants 3,000 years ago.

FOXH.a: The English Foxhound is one of the four foxhound breeds of dog. It is a cousin of the American Foxhound.
FOXH.h: The English Foxhound has been bred for over two hundred years, with the stud books dating back before 1800.

GDJK.a: The golden jackal, also called the common jackal, is a wolf-like canid that is native to Eurasia.

GLEN.a: The Glen of Imaal Terrier is a rare Irish dog breed from County Wicklow, Ireland, and one of four original Irish terrier breeds native to Ireland.

GOLD.a: The Golden Retriever is a Scottish breed of retriever dog of medium-large size.
GOLD.h: The Golden Retriever was developed in Scotland in the nineteenth century by Sir Dudley Marjoribanks (later to become Baron Tweedmouth) from Flat-coated Retrievers judiciously crossed with Tweed Water Spaniels and some other British dog breeds.

GORD.a: The Gordon Setter is a Scottish large breed of dog, a member of the setter family that also includes both the better-known Irish Setter and the English Setter.
GORD.h: Domesticated Dogs Finding Their Game by Scent, But Not Killing It, Being Chiefly Used in Aid of the Gun"

GPYR.a: The Pyrenean Mountain Dog is a French breed of livestock guardian dog.
GPYR.h: The French name Patou derives from pâtre, meaning shepherd. It is sometimes claimed that the breed’s ancestors — along with those of the closely related Pyrenean Mastiff — were white livestock guardian dogs brought from Asia during Roman times, linking them to the Maremmano-Abruzzese Sheepdog of Italy and the Kuvasz of Hungary.

GREE.a: The Greenland Dog is a breed of large dog of husky type. It is kept as a sled dog.
GREE.h: An Esquimaux bitch was exhibited at one of the earliest dog shows held in Darlington, Britain on 29 July 1875, which was reported in the Live Stock Journal and Fanciers Gazette published on 6 August 1875.

GREY.a: The Greyhound is a breed of dog and a sighthound. It is an ancient breed historically developed for hunting game by sight and speed, and has later been used in organised coursing and greyhound racing.
GREY.h: "The true origin of the Greyhound is unsure, but drawings of findings from the Çatalhöyük site in Turkey (6000 BC), the finding of a Greyhound-like dog in a funeral vase in the town of Fusa in Iran (4200 BC) or in rock art in Tassili (dated at 5000 – 2000 BC) indicate that the Greyhound is indeed one of the oldest breeds of dog."
GREY.ht: 71 to 76 centimetres (28 to 30 in; males), 68 to 71 centimetres (27 to 28 in; females)
GREY.wt: 27 to 40 kilograms (60 to 88 lb)* (males), 25 to 34 kilograms (55 to 75 lb)*; *Normal weight range (females)

GSD.a: The German Shepherd, also known in Britain as an Alsatian, is a German breed of working dog of medium to large size.
GSD.h: During the 1890s, attempts were being made to standardise dog breeds. Dogs were being bred to preserve traits that assisted in their job of herding sheep and protecting their flocks from predators.

GSHP.a: The German Shorthaired Pointer or Deutsch Kurzhaar is a German breed of continental pointing dog of Braque type.
GSHP.h: The pointing dog breeds of Europe all derive from the now-extinct Old Spanish Pointer, which spread through France and the Low Countries and reached the princely houses of the German-speaking world, where at first they were used in bird-hunting with nets or falcons, and later by huntsmen with guns.

GSMD.a: The Greater Swiss Mountain Dog is a dog breed which was developed in the Swiss Alps.
GSMD.h: The origin of the Greater Swiss Mountain Dog is not known. Beginning in 1515, the remote valleys of Switzerland were more or less isolated from world history for three centuries.

GSNZ.a: The Giant Schnauzer or Riesenschnauzer is a German breed of dog of Schnauzer type.
GSNZ.h: The origin of the breed name "Schnauzer" is not known, nor is it known when it came into use.

GWHP.a: The German Wirehaired Pointer or Deutsch Drahthaar is a German breed of pointing dog of Griffon type.
GWHP.h: The Deutsch Drahthaar was definitively accepted by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale in 1954.

HAVA.a: The Havanese, a bichon-type dog, is the national dog of Cuba, developed from the now extinct Blanquito de la Habana.
HAVA.h: The Havanese is a member of the bichon family of dogs. The progenitors of the breed are believed to have come from Tenerife.

HUSK.a: The Siberian Husky is a breed of medium-sized working sled dog. The breed belongs to the Spitz genetic family.
HUSK.h: The Chukotka Sled Dog is considered the progenitor to the Siberian Husky.

IBIZ.a: The Ibizan Hound is a lean, agile dog of the hound family. There are two hair types of the breed: smooth and wire.
IBIZ.h: DNA analysis indicates that the breed was formed recently from other breeds.

ICES.a: The Icelandic Sheepdog, is an Icelandic breed of dog of Nordic Spitz type.
ICES.h: The Icelandic Sheepdog is one of very few breeds of dog for which claims of ancient origin are demonstrably supported by both archaeological and written evidence.
ICES.ht: 46 centimetres (18 in; males), 42 centimetres (17 in; females)

INCA.a: The Peruvian Hairless Dog or Perro Sin Pelo del Perú is a Peruvian breed of hairless dog.
INCA.h: The Peruvian Hairless Dog is often perceived to be an Incan dog because it is known to have been kept during the Inca Empire (the Spaniards classified them as one of the six different breeds of dogs in the empire), and they were also kept as pets in pre-Inca cultures from the Peruvian northern coastal zone.

IRIT.a: The Irish Terrier is a dog breed from Ireland, one of many breeds of terrier.
IRIT.h: The breed's origin is not known. It is believed to have descended from the black and tan terrier-type dogs of Britain and Ireland, just like the Kerry Blue and Soft-coated Wheaten Terriers in Ireland or the Welsh, Lakeland and Scottish Terriers in Great Britain.

ISET.a: The Irish Setter is a setter, a breed of gundog, and family dog originating in Ireland.
ISET.h: One of the first references to the 'Setter,' or setting dog, in literature can be found in Caius's De Canibus Britannicis, which was published in 1570 (with a revised version published in 1576).

ITGY.a: The Italian Greyhound or Piccolo Levriero Italiano is an Italian breed of small sighthound.
ITGY.h: Small dogs of sighthound type have long been popular with European nobility and royalty.

IWOF.a: The Irish Wolfhound is a breed of large sighthound that has, by its presence and substantial size, inspired literature, poetry and mythology.
IWOF.h: In 391, there is a reference to large dogs by Quintus Aurelius Symmachus, a Roman consul who got seven "canes Scotici" as a gift to be used for fighting lions and bears, and who wrote "all Rome viewed (them) with wonder".

IWSP.a: The Irish Water Spaniel is a breed of dog that is the tallest of the spaniels.
IWSP.h: The modern breed as we know it was developed in Ireland in the 1830s. There is a strong case that the breed's ancestors originated in Persia and arrived in Ireland from Spain.

JACK.a: The Jack Russell Terrier is a British breed of small terrier. It is principally white-bodied and may have a smooth, rough, or broken coat, with markings of various colours.
JACK.h: The small white fox-working terriers were first bred by the Reverend John "Jack" Russell, a parson and hunting enthusiast born in 1795, and they can trace their origin to the now extinct English White Terrier.

KEES.a: The Keeshond is a medium-sized dog with a plush, two-layer coat of silver and black fur with a ruff and a curled tail.
KEES.h: The Keeshond was named after the 18th-century Dutch Patriot, Cornelis (Kees) de Gyselaer (spelled 'Gijzelaar' in Modern Dutch), leader of the rebellion against the House of Orange.

KELP.a: The Australian Kelpie, or simply Kelpie, is an Australian sheepdog capable of mustering and droving with little or no guidance.
KELP.h: The ancestors of most Kelpies were British dogs known loosely as collies (sometimes spelled colleys).

KERY.a: The Kerry Blue Terrier or Irish Blue Terrier is an Irish breed of dog of terrier type.
KERY.h: The Kerry Blue is first documented in 1847, when it was described as bluish slate in colour, marked with darker blotches and patches, and often with black about the legs and muzzle.

KOMO.a: The Komondor, also known as the Hungarian sheepdog, is a large, white-coloured Hungarian breed of livestock guardian dog with a long, corded coat.

KUVZ.a: The Kuvasz is a Hungarian breed of flock guardian dog. Mention of the breed can be found in old Hungarian texts.
KUVZ.h: Found in Western Anatolia, the Akbash dog breed is related to the Kuvasz, a Hungarian dog breed originating in Hungary.

LAB.a: The Labrador Retriever, also known simply as the Labrador or Lab, is a British breed of retriever gun dog.
LAB.h: The Labrador breed dates back to at least the 1830s, when St John's water dogs bred by European settlers in Newfoundland were first introduced to Britain from ships trading between Canada and Poole in Dorset.

LEON.a: The Leonberger is a German breed of large dog. The breed name derives from that of the city of Leonberg, in Baden-Württemberg, where it was bred in the mid-nineteenth century.
LEON.h: In the 1830s, Heinrich Essig, a dog breeder and seller and mayor of the town of Leonberg near Stuttgart in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, claimed to have created the Leonberger by crossing a female Landseer Newfoundland with a "barry" male from the Great St Bernard Hospice and Monastery (which would later create the Saint Bernard).

LHSA.a: The Lhasa Apso is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet. Traditionally the breed has been used as an interior watchdog.
LHSA.h: The Lhasa Apso is a thousand-year-old breed that historically served as sentinels at palaces and monasteries isolated high in the Himalayas of Tibet.

LMUN.a: The Large Münsterländer or Großer Münsterländer is a modern German breed of continental pointing dog of spaniel type.
LMUN.h: The pointing dog breeds of Europe all derive from the now-extinct Old Spanish Pointer, which spread through France and the Low Countries and reached the princely houses of the German-speaking world, where at first they were used in bird-hunting with nets or falcons, and later by huntsmen with guns.

MAAB.a: The Maremmano-Abruzzese Sheepdog is an Italian breed of livestock guardian dog.
MAAB.h: Descriptions of white flock guardian dogs are found in ancient Roman literature, in works such as those of Columella, Varro and Palladius.

MALT.a: Maltese dog refers both to an ancient variety of dwarf, white-coated dog breed from Italy and generally associated also with the island of Malta, and to a modern breed of similar dogs in the toy group, genetically related to the Bichon, Bolognese, and Havanese breeds.

MAST.a: The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.
MAST.h: There is a ceramic and paint sculpture of a mastiff-like dog from Mesopotamia region during the Kassite period (mid-2nd millennium B.C.).

MBLT.a: The Miniature Bull Terrier is a breed with origins in the extinct English White Terrier, the Dalmatian and the Bulldog.
MBLT.h: When the Bull Terrier breed was first created in 19th century England, it was about the same size as the Miniature Bull Terrier.

MNTY.a: The Toy Manchester Terrier is a breed of dog, categorized as a terrier.
MNTY.h: The Manchester Terrier, from which the Toy Manchester Terrier was bred, was developed in the 19th century from crosses between an old Black and Tan Terrier with the Whippet, along with other breeds, primarily for rat-catching.

MPIN.a: The Miniature Pinscher or Zwergpinscher is a German breed of small dog of Pinscher type.
MPIN.h: The dogs were used traditionally to hunt mice, lizards, small birds, rabbits, pests and vermin and were hunting dogs.

MPOO.a: The Poodle, called the Pudel in German and the Caniche in French, is a breed of water dog.
MPOO.h: Most cynologists believe the Poodle originated in Germany in the Middle Ages, from a dog similar to today's Standard Poodle.

MSNZ.a: The Miniature Schnauzer is a German breed of small dog of Schnauzer type.
MSNZ.h: Neither the origin of the breed name, nor when it came into use, is known.

MXOL.a: The Xoloitzcuintle is one of several breeds of hairless dog. It is found in standard, intermediate, and miniature sizes.
MXOL.h: Ceramic sculptures of a hairless breed of dog have been found in burial sites in ancient West Mexico.

NEAP.a: The Neapolitan Mastiff or Mastino Napoletano is an Italian breed of large dog of mastiff type.
NEAP.h: The Neapolitan Mastiff derives from the traditional catch and guard dogs of Southern Italy.

NELK.a: The Norwegian Elkhound is one of the Northern Spitz-type breeds of dog and is the National Dog of Norway.
NELK.h: The breed is popular in Sweden where it has always been highly prized as a hunting dog.

NEWF.a: The Newfoundland is a large breed of working dog. They can be black, grey, brown, or black and white.
NEWF.h: Genomic analysis indicates that Newfoundlands are related to the Irish Water Spaniel, Labrador Retriever, and Curly-Coated Retriever.

NORF.a: The Norfolk Terrier is a British breed of dog. Prior to gaining recognition as an independent breed in 1964, it was a variety of the Norwich Terrier, distinguished from the "prick eared" Norwich by its "drop ears".
NORF.h: In the 1880s, British sportsmen developed a working terrier of East Anglia in eastern England.

NOWT.a: The Norwich Terrier is a breed of dog originating in England, and was bred to hunt small rodents.
NOWT.h: Fox hunting terriers resembling the Norwich have been described since the 19th century.

NSDT.a: The Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever is a medium-sized gun dog bred primarily for hunting.
NSDT.h: The breed was developed in the Acadian community of Little River Harbour in Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia around the beginning of the 19th century.

OES.a: The Old English Sheepdog is a large breed of dog that emerged in England from early types of herding dog.
OES.h: The Old English Sheepdog comes from the pastoral type dogs of England.
OES.ht: 61 centimetres (24 in) and upwards (males), 56 centimetres (22 in) and upwards (females)
OES.wt: 36–46 kilograms (79–101 lb; males), 30–40 kilograms (66–88 lb; females)

OTTR.a: The Otterhound is an English dog breed. It is a scent hound and is currently recognised by the Kennel Club as a Vulnerable Native Breed with around 600 animals worldwide.

PAPI.a: The Épagneul Nain Continental or Continental Toy Spaniel is a Belgian and French breed of dog of spaniel type and of miniature or toy size.
PAPI.h: Lapdogs of miniature spaniel type appear in paintings from the sixteenth century onwards, in the works of Titian, Paolo Veronese, Pierre Mignard, Gonzales Coques, Antoine Watteau and Jean-Honoré Fragonard among others.

PARS.a: The Parson Russell Terrier is an English breed of small white terrier that was the original Fox Terrier of the 18th century.
PARS.h: This type of small white terrier dates back to the work of the Reverend John Russell, born in 1795.

PBGV.a: The Petit Basset Griffon Vendéen is a French breed of small dog of scent hound type, bred to trail hares in bramble-filled terrain of the Vendée district of France.

PEKE.a: The Pekingese is a breed of toy dog, originating in China. The breed was favored by royalty of the Chinese Imperial court as a companion dog, and its name refers to the city of Beijing (Peking) where the Forbidden City is located.
PEKE.h: The breed emerged in China from several kinds of small dog owned by aristocratic families.

PEMB.a: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a cattle herding dog breed that originated in Pembrokeshire, Wales.
PEMB.h: While the Cardigan Welsh Corgi is thought to originate with the arrival of Celtic culture (around 1200 BCE), the Pembroke Welsh Corgi is more commonly stated to originate with the Flemish plantations that were settled in Pembrokeshire following the Norman Invasion of Wales.

PHAR.a: The Pharaoh Hound or Kelb tal-Fenek is a Maltese breed of warren hound.
PHAR.h: The Kelb tal-Fenek is a traditional breed of rural Malta. As the English-language exonym suggests, it is sometimes claimed that the Pharaoh Hound descends from the dogs shown in the tomb paintings of Ancient Egypt.

POM.a: The Pomeranian is a breed of dog of the Spitz type that is named for the Pomerania region in north-west Poland and north-east Germany in Central Europe.
POM.h: The Pomeranian is considered to be descended from the German Spitz. The breed is thought to have acquired its name by association with the area known as Pomerania which is located in northern Poland and Germany along the Baltic Sea.

PTWD.a: The Portuguese Water Dog, also known as the Algarvian Water Dog, or Portuguese Fishing Dog, is a breed of dog that originated from the Algarve region of Portugal.
PTWD.h: The Portuguese Water Dog and the Poodle appear to have developed from the same ancient genetic pool; at one time the Poodle was a longer-coated dog, as is one variety of the Portuguese Water Dog.

PUG.a: The Pug is a breed of dog with the physically distinctive features of a wrinkly, short-muzzled face, and curled tail.
PUG.h: The ancestor of the Pug was a dog called the Lo-Chiang-Sze, or Lo-Sze in its shortened form.

PULI.a: The Puli is a small-medium breed of Hungarian herding dog known for its long, corded coat.
PULI.h: The Magyars probably brought the Puli to Hungary in the 9th Century when they invaded westwards from Siberia, and it has been a sheepdog on the Hungarian plain since then.

PUMI.a: The Pumi is a medium-small breed of sheep dog from Hungary. They are capable herding dogs, able to gather and work close to farm stock, particularly sheep, to keep them under control.
PUMI.h: This breed emerged in the 17th–18th Century as a descendent from the Puli, German Spitz, French Briard and some type of terrier.

RATT.a: The Rat Terrier is an American dog breed with a background as a farm dog and hunting companion.
RATT.h: The earliest-known record of a rat-catching dog is that of "Hatch", whose remains were recovered from the Mary Rose, the flagship of Henry VIII, sunk in 1545 and raised in 1982.

REDB.a: The Redbone Coonhound is an American breed of hunting dog. As a coonhound, the Redbone is primarily a hunter of small game that hide in trees, such as raccoons, opossums, and squirrels, but is also capable of handling big game like bears and cougars.
REDB.h: In the early 19th century, Scottish immigrants brought red-colored foxhounds to Georgia, which would later become the foundation stock of today's modern-day Redbone.

RHOD.a: The Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large dog breed originally bred in Southern Africa.
RHOD.h: The Khoikhoi people who lived in the Cape Peninsula when the Dutch began trading with the area during the mid 17th century, had a hunting dog which was described by Europeans as absolutely fearless and ferocious when acting as a guard dog.

ROTT.a: The Rottweiler is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.
ROTT.h: According to the FCI Standard, the Rottweiler is considered to be one of the oldest surviving dog breeds.

SALU.a: The Saluki or Arabian hound or Persian hound is a standardised breed developed from sighthounds – dogs that hunt primarily by sight rather than strong scent – that was once used by nomadic tribes to run down game animals.
SALU.h: The Saluki's ancestors were historically bred in the Fertile Crescent, where agriculture originated.

SAMO.a: The Samoyed is a breed of herding dog with a thick, white, double-layered coat.
SAMO.h: The progenitor of the Samoyeds was the Nenets Herding Laika, a reindeer herding spitz commonly used throughout the Arctic, especially the Nenets people, who were pejoratively referred to as Samoyeds at that time.
SAMO.wt: 20–30 kilograms (44–66 lb; males), 16–20 kilograms (35–44 lb; females)

SCOT.a: The Scottish Terrier, popularly called the Scottie, is a breed of dog.
SCOT.h: Initial grouping of several of the highland terriers (including the Scottie) under the generic name Skye Terriers caused some confusion in the breed's lineage.

SCWT.a: The soft-coated Wheaten Terrier is a pure-breed terrier originating from Ireland.
SCWT.h: The Wheaten was bred in Ireland for over two hundred years to be an all-purpose farm dog whose duties included herding, watching and guarding livestock, and vermin hunting and killing.

SHAR.a: The Shar Pei is a dog breed from southern China. Traditionally kept as a property guardian, the Shar Pei was driven to the brink of extinction in the 20th century.
SHAR.h: There are no records indicating the origins of the Shar Pei, although it closely resembles effigies of an un-wrinkled type of guard dog kept in southern China during the Han dynasty; some believe the modern breed, along with the Chow Chow, descends from these dogs.

SHIB.a: The Shiba Inu is a breed of hunting dog from Japan. A small-to-medium breed, it is the smallest of the six original dog breeds native to Japan.
SHIB.h: The Shiba Inu has been identified as a basal breed that predates the emergence of the modern breeds in the 19th century.

SHIH.a: The Shih Tzu is a toy dog or pet dog breed originating from Tibet and believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso.
SHIH.h: One theory is that the Shih Tzu descended from a cross between the Pekingese and Lhasa Apso.

SILK.a: The Australian Silky Terrier or simply Silky Terrier is a small breed of dog of the terrier dog type.
SILK.h: The ancestors of the Australian Silky Terrier include the Yorkshire Terrier and the Australian Terrier (which descends from the rough coated type terriers brought from Great Britain to Australia in the early 19th century); few records indicate whether early dogs were just Australian Terriers born with silky fur, or whether there was an attempt to create a separate breed.

SKIP.a: A Schipperke is a small breed of dog that is believed to have originated in the 1600s in Flanders.
SKIP.h: The earlier common references to Schipperkes suggest that they may have originated in the 1600s in Flanders.

SLOU.a: The Sloughi, Arabian Greyhound, or Berber Greyhound is an ancient breed of domesticated dog, a member of the sighthound family.
SLOU.h: The Sloughi has existed for centuries in North Africa, primarily in Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt.

SPIN.a: The Spinone Italiano is an Italian breed of hunting dog, traditionally used for tracking, for pointing and for retrieving game.
SPIN.h: The origins of the Spinone are unknown. Rough-haired dogs of pointer type have been present in the Italian peninsula at least since the Renaissance.

SPOO.a: The Poodle, called the Pudel in German and the Caniche in French, is a breed of water dog.
SPOO.h: Most cynologists believe the Poodle originated in Germany in the Middle Ages, from a dog similar to today's Standard Poodle.

SSHP.a: The Shetland Sheepdog, also known as the Sheltie, is a breed of herding dog that originated in the Shetland Islands of Scotland.
SSHP.h: Unlike many miniature breeds that resemble their larger counterparts, this breed was not developed simply by selectively breeding the Rough Collie for smaller and smaller size.

SSNZ.a: The Standard Schnauzer or Mittelschnauzer is a German breed of dog in the Pinscher and Schnauzer group.
SSNZ.h: Neither the origin of the breed name, nor when it came into use, is known.

STAF.a: The Staffordshire Bull Terrier, also called the Staffy or Stafford, is a purebred dog of small to medium size in the terrier group that originated in the northern parts of Birmingham and in Staffordshire, for which it is named.
STAF.h: The unregulated breeding history and inconsistent genetic makeup of the Stafford's early ancestry have led to misconceptions about its origins.

STBD.a: The St. Bernard or Saint Bernard is a breed of very large working dog from the Western Alps; they were originally bred for rescue work by the hospice of the Great St Bernard Pass on the Italian-Swiss border, with Switzerland recognized as its country of origin by the FCI.

SVAL.a: The Swedish Vallhund, also known as the Västgötaspets and Swedish cow dog, is a breed of dog native to Sweden.
SVAL.h: The Swedish Vallhund is an ancient, national dog breed of Sweden and may date back to the 8th or 9th century.

TIBM.a: The Tibetan Mastiff is a large Tibetan dog breed. Its double coat is medium to long, subject to climate, and found in a wide variety of colors, including solid black, black and tan, various shades of red and bluish-gray, and sometimes with white markings around its neck, chest and legs.
TIBM.h: Originally these dogs were used to protect Buddhist monasteries and monks of Tibet from animals such as bears, wolves and snow leopards.

TIBS.a: The Tibetan Spaniel is a breed of assertive, small dogs originating in Tibet.
TIBS.h: Small monastery dogs, thought to be early representatives of the Tibetan Spaniel, loyally trailed behind their Lama masters and came to be regarded as "Little Lions" owing to their resemblance to the Snow Lions—a variation of the Chinese guardian lions—that gave them great value and prestige.

TIBT.a: The Tibetan Terrier is a medium-sized breed of dog that originated in Tibet.
TIBT.h: Tibetan Terriers have been bred and raised in monasteries of Tibet for 2,000 years.

TPOO.a: The Poodle, called the Pudel in German and the Caniche in French, is a breed of water dog.
TPOO.h: Most cynologists believe the Poodle originated in Germany in the Middle Ages, from a dog similar to today's Standard Poodle.

TURV.a: The Belgian Shepherd, also known as the Belgian Sheepdog or the Chien de Berger Belge, is a Belgian breed of herding dog of medium size.
TURV.h: The Belgian Shepherd descends from the same common type of herding dog as similar Western European breeds such as the Bouvier des Ardennes, the Dutch Shepherd and the German Shepherd, and for centuries was used by Belgian shepherds for this task.

TYFX.a: The Toy Fox Terrier is a small terrier breed of dog, directly descended from the larger Smooth Fox Terrier but since 1936, it has been registered in the United States with the UKC as a separate breed.
TYFX.h: The Toy Fox Terrier is believed to have originated in the United States in the early 1900s.

VIZS.a: The Vizsla, also known as Hungarian Vizsla, Magyar Vizsla or Hungarian Pointer, is a dog breed from Hungary and belongs to the Fédération Cynologique Internationale (FCI) group 7, the Canadian Kennel Club (CKC) group 1, and the American Kennel Club.
VIZS.h: The first written reference to the Vizsla dog breed has been recorded in the Illustrated Vienna Chronicle prepared on order of King Louis I of Hungary by the Carmelite Friars in 1357.

VPIN.a: The Volpino Italiano or Volpino is an Italian breed of dog of Spitz type.
VPIN.h: Small Spitz-type dogs resembling the modern Volpino have been identified in a number of paintings, of which the earliest may be St. Augustine in His Study by Vittore Carpaccio, painted in the Scuola di San Giorgio degli Schiavoni in Venice in 1502.

WEIM.a: The Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.
WEIM.h: Many theories of the origin of the Weimaraner have been advanced, but there are few documented historical facts; silver-grey dogs are shown in paintings by Antoon van Dyck in the seventeenth century and by Jean-Baptiste Oudry in the eighteenth.

WFOX.a: The Wire Fox Terrier is a breed of dog, one of many terrier breeds. It is a Fox Terrier, and although it bears a resemblance to the Smooth Fox Terrier, they are believed to have been developed separately.
WFOX.h: The Wire Fox Terrier was developed in England by fox hunting enthusiasts and is believed to be descended from a now-extinct rough-coated, black-and-tan working terrier of Wales, Derbyshire, and Durham.

WHIP.a: The Whippet is a British breed of sighthound. It closely resembles the Greyhound and the smaller Italian Greyhound, and is intermediate between them in size.
WHIP.h: Whippets, like all other sighthounds, were bred to hunt using their sight-driven prey instinct, coursing game in open areas at high speeds.

WHPG.a: The Wirehaired Pointing Griffon is a breed of dog used in hunting as a gundog.
WHPG.h: Eduard Karel Korthals is credited with the breed around 1873. Korthals' dream was to create the ideal versatile gun dog; one with extreme resiliency, vigor, and devotion to its master.

WHWT.a: The West Highland White Terrier is a Scottish dog breed with a distinctive white harsh coat and somewhat soft white undercoat.
WHWT.h: Scottish white terriers were recorded as early as during the reign of James VI of Scotland, who reigned between 1567 and 1625.

WOLF.a: The wolf, also known as the grey wolf or gray wolf, is a canine native to Eurasia and North America.

XIGO.a: The Xigou, also known as Xiquan, Xiliegou, Chinese Hound, Kuaiquan, and Chinese Xiquan, is a rare breed of sighthound native to China.

XOLO.a: The Xoloitzcuintle is one of several breeds of hairless dog. It is found in standard, intermediate, and miniature sizes.
XOLO.h: Ceramic sculptures of a hairless breed of dog have been found in burial sites in ancient West Mexico.

YORK.a: The Yorkshire Terrier, also known as a Yorkie, is a British breed of toy dog of terrier type.
YORK.h: The Yorkshire Terrier originated in Yorkshire. In the mid-nineteenth century, workers from Scotland came to Yorkshire in search of work and brought with them several varieties of terrier dogs.
